note: criteria 1, 3, 4, 5 — 4 of 5. Criterion 1 (quantitative grounding) satisfied: workforce TRIR of 0.36 and LTIR of 0.08 incidents per 200,000 hours worked reported for 2024, broken out by employee and contractor; fatality counts for employees (0) and contractors (0) in 2024 also stated on p.7; all figures carry explicit units. Criterion 2 (target-bound) not satisfied: no named safety target with a baseline year and target year is disclosed; safety performance metrics are included in executive compensation goals (p.66) but no quantitative improvement target with baseline and target year is stated for TRIR, LTIR, or fatalities. Criterion 3 (methodology disclosed) satisfied: p.57 footnote explicitly states the OSHA industry-standard measurement formula (incidents multiplied by 200,000 divided by hours worked) as the calculation method for both TRIR and LTIR; p.74 confirms this by showing the full calculation with actual numerators, denominators, and hours worked figures for employees, contractors, and combined workforce separately — this satisfies the handbook requirement for an explicit calculation or assessment methodology including workforce scope boundary (employees and contractors tracked separately). Criterion 4 (time horizon) satisfied: 2024 anchor year is explicit across all safety tables; the five-year column headers on p.7 (2024, 2023, 2022, 2021, 2020) establish the reporting period. Criterion 5 (progress tracking) satisfied: workforce TRIR series 0.45 / 0.40 / 0.51 / 0.46 / 0.36 and workforce LTIR series 0.13 / 0.11 / 0.17 / 0.12 / 0.08 for 2020–2024 provide anchor year plus four prior years for both headline metrics; fatality series also covers 2020–2024 on p.7. Handbook pitfall check: criterion 3 confirmed satisfied — spans include both the OSHA methodology statement (p.57) and the actual formula with raw incident counts and hours worked (p.74), establishing workforce scope (employees vs contractors tracked separately) as part of methodology. Contractor inclusion note: p.57 footnote states 'We work closely with our contractors to capture the hours worked by their employees and subcontractors' — contractor hours are explicitly tracked alongside employee hours, satisfying the handbook note that contractor safety belongs in O7 when hours are tracked alongside employees. forward_looking set false: no future safety targets or projections appear in selected spans. assured set false: no named third-party assurer linked to safety data in selected spans.
